_legend: jb = Jackbox-style party designer persona; mp = Mario Party-style designer persona. verdict ∈ keep | tweak | cut. Functional review personas based on the studios' public design philosophy — not real named individuals.

Order Up.jb_note: Icebreaker DNA is perfect for strangers; the conversation round must be structured, not optional — give every player a 10-second 'defend your order' turn before guesses, and reveal one drink at a time so the room reacts to each person.
Order Up.mp_note: Win state ('most right') needs a live scoreboard and a speed tiebreak; cap at 8 (16 drinks is unreadable). Reveal beat: big check/cross rain per guess.

Split or Steal.jb_note: Zero rules explanation and the best spectator moment on the list — but 'stolen from by a stranger, eliminated' is the one outcome that humiliates rather than amuses. Make stakes comedic (loser wears a badge / does a 10-second dare), and give the 14 watchers a job: predict the outcome.
Split or Steal.mp_note: Instantly readable (two buttons). Run as a bracket so everyone gets a chair; audience bets for coins fix the sit-out; the reveal animation IS the payoff — invest there.

Sheep Raid.jb_note: Not our genre, but it works: rules fit in one sentence ('grab sheep, pen them, raid theirs'), failure is funny (your pen gets robbed), strangers can play it without talking.
Sheep Raid.mp_note: Pen counts are the score — readable. Add a golden sheep (worth 3) in the last 60 s as the comeback beat, and a shared countdown everyone can see. Our favourite of the signature three.

Trivia (first to 3).jb_note: No room in it: nobody reacts to anyone. Trivia is only a vehicle — fold the questions into Majority Rules / 'who's most likely to' where the answer is a person.
Trivia (first to 3).mp_note: Readable and fast, but knowledge decides it — mismatched players never win. Needs a luck layer (double-or-nothing final, random steals) or it's a filler only.

Trivia: Majority Rules.jb_note: This is our bread and butter — 'what would the room say' is a personality reveal. Show the answers WITH names on the reveal ('who said gorilla?!') and it becomes about people. The sim's zero-interaction flag is about direction, not value: add a bonus for guessing a specific person's answer and the flag disappears.
Trivia: Majority Rules.mp_note: Readable, luck-heavy (guessing the room levels the field), scales to 16. Needs a minimum of 3 and an odd-count or tiebreak rule for even splits.

Trivia: Higher or Lower.jb_note: Pure knowledge, no reveal, no people. Cut.
Trivia: Higher or Lower.mp_note: Fine 10-second filler on a shared screen if everyone answers together and the reveal is loud — but as a standalone game it has no payoff.

Draw My Thing.jb_note: Proven format; bad drawings are the joke, so failure is funny and strangers relax. Fix the scale problem the sim found by drawing SIMULTANEOUSLY then guessing round-robin on phone — 16 players no longer means 8 minutes.
Draw My Thing.mp_note: Drawing skill dominates. Handicap rounds (non-dominant hand, 8-second limit, draw with eyes closed) level it and are funnier. Points to drawer AND guesser, speed tiebreak.

Caption This (제목 짓기).jb_note: Quiplash-shaped: zero explanation, the reveal is everyone reacting to one answer, strangers are safe behind anonymity until the vote. Minimum 3 (2 always ties — sim agrees).
Caption This (제목 짓기).mp_note: Readable (votes). Use a head-to-head bracket vote instead of plurality to kill the ties the sim found, and animate the vote count.

Performance.jb_note: Best spectator moment on the list, but forced performing humiliates shy strangers. Make it opt-in per round, or pair performers, or flip it: the room DUBS a 10-second mime (the captions are the joke, not the acting).
Performance.mp_note: Score the guessers too so the performer isn't the only one on the hook; 3 random performers per game, not everyone — 16 performers is 12 minutes.

Split Clue.jb_note: Keep-Talking energy: the whole game is two strangers talking, and miscommunication is funny. One sentence of rules. Low spectator value but that's fine for a catalog pick.
Split Clue.mp_note: Readable (first pair done). Rotate puzzle difficulty randomly so the same pair doesn't always win.

Boss Fight.jb_note: Tap-fest with no personality and no reveal. If it survives: make each player's ANSWER the attack (type an insult; the room votes; the best one does the damage).
Boss Fight.mp_note: The spectacle (a shared HP bar dying) is very us, but nobody loses and nobody's MVP. Add last-hit bonus, random power-up turns, and a contribution podium.

Death Tag / Cops & Robbers.jb_note: Not our genre. Physical contact with strangers is the comfort issue — tag by phone proximity (the app already has it), never by touch.
Death Tag / Cops & Robbers.mp_note: Readable, everyone stays in (snowball), great at 8–16, last-survivor drama. Exactly what we'd ship.

Timebomb / Hot Potato.jb_note: Zero explanation, the loser's phone going off is the laugh, proximity toss means no touching. Keep.
Timebomb / Hot Potato.mp_note: Readable, luck-ish, loud payoff (the boom), any headcount. Best catalog minigame on the list.

Tile Wars.jb_note: Needs a map and an explanation; no moment where the room reacts to a person. Not ours.
Tile Wars.mp_note: Coverage is readable, teams scale, add random power tiles and a shrinking-map endgame so the 1v1 'teams never met' case can't happen.

Infection Zones.jb_note: Physical, no laugh beat, requires a map. Not ours.
Infection Zones.mp_note: Inside/outside a shrinking circle is instantly readable, zone placement is luck, elimination is drama, 4–16 scales. Keep.

Five Buttons.jb_note: Not a game — a 20-second DECIDER. Everyone watches one person press; the buzz is the laugh. Use it between games to pick who goes first / who pays. The sim is right that it's zero-interaction as a game.
Five Buttons.mp_note: Pure Chance Time. Keep it as the tiebreaker / interstitial, never as a headline game.

31 (Nim).mp_note: Skill decides it with perfect play and three-plus players is kingmaking. Cut.

Truth or Dare.jb_note: As-is it's not a game (no win). Its Jackbox form: everyone answers the truth question anonymously, the room votes who said it. Dares opt-in only with strangers.
Truth or Dare.mp_note: No win condition, nothing to read. Cut unless scored.

Liar Game / Mafia.jb_note: Fibbage / Fakin' It DNA. Time-box the discussion, give the liar a category hint, reveal with a drumroll.
Liar Game / Mafia.mp_note: Readable only at the vote; the middle is talk. Put a visible 45-second timer on the discussion and a vote-count reveal.

Tee Game (photo + slogan).jb_note: Tee K.O. is literally ours. Minimum 4 so pairings stay surprising; bracket vote to kill ties.
Tee Game (photo + slogan).mp_note: Random pairing is luck — levels the field. Readable. Keep.

Guess the Number (timing imposter).jb_note: The imposter layer is the interesting half and it belongs with Catch the Imposter. The timing-stop alone is a fine 15-second palate cleanser.
Guess the Number (timing imposter).mp_note: Stop-at-5.00 is a classic reflex minigame — readable, quick, luck-ish. Ship that alone; the discussion/vote layer slows it down.

Catch the Imposter.jb_note: Fakin' It shape. Force one sentence from each player before the vote (answers shown with names) so strangers can't sit silent — fixes the sim's 'silent-completable' flag.
Catch the Imposter.mp_note: Readable at the vote, luck in who's imposter, scales to 16 with two imposters. Keep.

Rival Teams (generic).jb_note: A framework, not a game — nothing to react to until a task exists.
Rival Teams (generic).mp_note: Superseded by Sheep Raid, which is the concrete version. Cut.

Scavenger (planted object).jb_note: Physical pre-setup, no room, no reveal. Cut.
Scavenger (planted object).mp_note: No readable win state, slow, doesn't scale. Cut (handcrafted-quest tier only).

Race / Manhunt-Tag.jb_note: Death Tag does the same thing without the tagged players sitting out bored.
Race / Manhunt-Tag.mp_note: Sit-out is the cardinal sin. Death Tag supersedes it.

Accuracy / Long Jump.jb_note: A skill show-off that embarrasses the less athletic stranger. Cut.
Accuracy / Long Jump.mp_note: Pure skill, the top athlete always wins (sim: 87%). Cut unless a random multiplier hides it.

Team Challenge (2p coop physical).jb_note: Undefined. Its concrete forms are already on the list (Split Clue for talk, Sheep Raid for bodies). Define a task or drop the placeholder.
Team Challenge (2p coop physical).mp_note: Two-player synced button-mash / mirror-move is a classic minigame — but pick the actual task; as a framework it can't ship.

Hide and Seek.jb_note: Long, sit-out, and a safety problem with strangers in a city. Cut.
Hide and Seek.mp_note: Sit-out plus a win state you can't see. Cut.

Consensus (debate to agree).jb_note: A conversation starter, not a game. Give it a twist — one secret dissenter who wins by steering the group wrong — and it becomes a game.
Consensus (debate to agree).mp_note: No winner, no readable state. Cut.
